The new rules, all in `workflow-check.ts`:
- **Globals as values.** A free global appears only as the callee of a direct call or as the object of a member call or read. It cannot be assigned, passed, returned, spread, put in an array or object, destructured, or used as an operand. Exceptions: `args` (plain readable data) and `undefined`, `NaN`, `Infinity`. Calling a global that is not a function (`Math()`, `Object(x)`) is refused.
- **Per-global member lists.**
  - Calls: `Object.keys|values|entries|fromEntries`, `Array.isArray|from|of`, `JSON.stringify|parse`, a short `Math` list, `Number.isInteger|isFinite|isNaN|parseFloat|parseInt`, and `Promise.all|allSettled|race|resolve|reject`.
  - Reads: the `Math` and `Number` numeric constants.
  - Not on any list: `assign`, `freeze`, `seal`, `defineProperty`, `defineProperties`, `setPrototypeOf`, `preventExtensions`, `create`, `groupBy`. No built-in can be rewritten, directly or through an alias.
- **Budget.** Only `budget.total`, `budget.spent()` and `budget.remaining()`; the old "any method of budget" exemption is gone. `budget` as a value is refused.
- **Methods.** A method (`map`, `push`, …) is called where it is read; reading one without calling it is refused (`const f = xs.push`, `[1].map(xs.push)`). The callback methods (`map`, `forEach`, `filter`, `find`, `findIndex`, `some`, `every`, `flatMap`) take one argument, so no `this` can be passed; `Array.from` takes at most two. `assign` and `freeze` left the instance list.
- **Writes.** Member assignment or update, and `x.y++`, are allowed only on a name that holds nothing but data the script built. Every value it is set to must be an object or array literal, an `agent()` result, data read from `args`, a result of an allowed data method, or another such name. A parameter, loop variable, function, global or call result is refused. This is evaluated after the walk, so a write from a function to a module-level name declared later now works (one of the optional findings).

Behavior changes to know:
- `log`, `phase` and other function globals can no longer be passed as callbacks (`.then(log)`); call them inside an arrow instead.
- Writing into a loop variable (`for (const row of args.entries) { row.done = true }`) or a parameter is refused.
- `${budget}` in a template is refused; use `budget.remaining()`.
- The `FULL_SCRIPT` test script was updated accordingly.
